package hasher_test

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/navidrome/navidrome/utils/hasher"
	. "github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2"
	. "github.com/onsi/gomega"
)

func TestHasher(t *testing.T) {
	RegisterFailHandler(Fail)
	RunSpecs(t, "Hasher Suite")
}

var _ = Describe("HashFunc", func() {
	const input = "123e4567e89b12d3a456426614174000"

	It("hashes the input and returns the sum", func() {
		hashFunc := hasher.HashFunc()
		sum := hashFunc("1", input)
		Expect(sum > 0).To(BeTrue())
	})

	It("hashes the input, reseeds and returns a different sum", func() {
		hashFunc := hasher.HashFunc()
		sum := hashFunc("1", input)
		hasher.Reseed("1")
		sum2 := hashFunc("1", input)
		Expect(sum).NotTo(Equal(sum2))
	})

	It("keeps different hashes for different ids", func() {
		hashFunc := hasher.HashFunc()
		sum := hashFunc("1", input)
		sum2 := hashFunc("2", input)

		Expect(sum).NotTo(Equal(sum2))

		Expect(sum).To(Equal(hashFunc("1", input)))
		Expect(sum2).To(Equal(hashFunc("2", input)))
	})
})

item.text: `maphash.Seed` can’t be reconstructed from a supplied string, so the current seed map can’t restore an earlier value. I’ll store seed strings per ID, use a deterministic hash for explicit seeds, and keep automatic initialization and reseeding for IDs without a supplied seed.

item.text:
Implemented deterministic per-ID seeding in [hasher.go](/app/utils/hasher/hasher.go). Setting a seed now reproduces the same hash, reseeding changes it, and restoring the seed restores the original hash. IDs without a seed initialize automatically.

Added coverage in [hasher_test.go](/app/utils/hasher/hasher_test.go). `go test -race ./utils/hasher` and `git diff --check` passed.
